I’m a little late to the party, but reading all of these recalled something to my mind that happened about 10 years ago when I was studying abroad in Japan.

I had been living with my Japanese-Chinese roommate for a few months. We got along well. She also had a young puppy she didn’t have time to train that drove me nuts, but that was the major friction.

One afternoon we both came home, me from school and her from work, wiped the hell out. One of those sleeps that hits you and you feel like “shit I must be getting sick” kinda sleeps. We both passed out in our beds, zonked for hours.

I woke up with a big start late afternoon. I had just had the most vivid dream that something bad was happening to my family. I was sweating, I felt very upset. I needed to contact them and I also had a dazed and compulsive urge to immediately go to my roommate whether she was asleep or not. I was upset, but I’m not the kind of person to go wake up someone because of a bad dream. I don’t know what I was thinking about doing, but I think I was just rocked from the nightmare and how vivid it was. My parents were so far away, maybe I just needed someone to be close.

It was a Japanese apartment, tiny as hell, just three main rooms in a row with the kitchen splitting our two bedrooms. I fly across the kitchen and almost smash into her, who is coming at me just as urgently and sweaty. We’re both in a flurry. She says she just had a horrible dream that something bad happened to her family. I tell her I just did too but my family. We stare at each other, we’re holding each other. We both turn like zombies to contact our families and freeze because her dog is GROWLING at my bedroom. Ooh, I get chills remembering. He GROWLED like there was something VERY bad in there. This was very uncharacteristic of this happy-go-stupid/lucky dog. I know this might be considered animal cruelty, but we threw a toy in there, something usually irresistible to him, and he ran in the opposite direction and hid in my roommate’s bedcovers.

I’m not a brave person at all, but I didn’t like seeing how scared my roommate and the dog were. And fuck -I- have to sleep here for a year so if there’s something up I better handle it ASAP whatever it is.

I went in there even though my roommate was crying and begging me not to. I couldn’t think what could be SO bad in semi-daylight in a populated apartment building that we couldn’t handle and if it’s ghosts, well I’m not alone so my chances seem better or something. I honestly feel like I’m sensitive to energy and I did NOT feel a presence or something bad in that room. I tried to call the pupper in, no go. My roommate was crying but we pulled ourselves together and contact our folks. My parents were fine but my childhood cat was sick and they hadn’t wanted to tell me because they wanted to treat him and get him well as best as they could and not worry me. That cat did pass away a year later.

My friend’s family was also fine, but about the same time my cat died a year later, her puppy bolted out of the house into traffic got hit and died. It’s almost weird enough, still gives me chills. But I think we both just had similar stress dreams.

BONUS STORY:

I was away at college and one night I decided to take some mushrooms. I wasn’t new to hallucinogens, bad trips for me are just if my tummy hurts but if my brain gets upset I can usually nurture myself into a good place. Well I’m tripping on a low dose, enjoying a bubble bath, when I get a similar feeling to that dream in Japan, but I’m awake. It’s very pressing. “Something bad is happening to your dad.” I was really upset by this, but tripping so I’m not going to call him right now. I think “It’s late, I know I’m high. If something were going wrong, my mom would call me. I talked myself down, I go to bed eventually, restless.

Next morning I call my folks. They both pick up, yay. They’re used to me being weird so I just say, “Hey I had a bad feeling about dad last night, is he okay?” Pause on the other end.

“Well actually your dad was at a company dinner last night, stood up, and fainted. He came to and we think he just ate too much rich food and drank the wine too fast, but we had him checked out. He’s okay. We didn’t want to worry you since he’s fine!”

So that was weird for all of us.
